calls.reason: The only measurement, the Harvard Misinformation Review study, finds a modest drop in source quality, with low-quality link volume stable or falling. That neither clearly confirms nor refutes 'much, much worse'.
The Community Notes preprint shows AI posts got slower first notes but reached consensus more often. The later AI note writers show adaptation, not proof of overload, so the evidence is mixed.
The GPT-3 study shows near-human detection of false tweets (0.89 vs 0.92), which cuts against 'suck', but its timing is unclear and unmatched generation was never established.
This is an open-ended forecast. Studies show larger models doing better on truthfulness and fact-checking, while others show persistent failures, and none isolates scale alone.
The forecast is hedged and undated. Epoch shows prices falling, but the only volume data (synthetic media on X) rose then stabilized and was mostly harmless, with no measure of total misinformation.

ReAct (Oct 2022) showed PaLM-540B checking FEVER claims against retrieved Wikipedia evidence, beating chain-of-thought prompting. That is a working, though imperfect, way to reason against a reference standard.
